title: Quarterly roadmap: cohort-driven commitment scenarios for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define quarterly commitment scenarios for the Hosted API + Model Catalog that map model lineups to customer cohorts, contingency triggers, and experiment lanes. This ticket synthesizes capacity planning, canary windows, OKR alignment, and decision rules so Engineering, Ops, and Sales can commit to a lean but resilient model rotation plan for Q2.

Scope:
- Produce 3 commitment scenarios (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) with explicit model lineup per endpoint tier.
- For each scenario, define: cohort mappings (enterprise, mid-market, AI-native), regional priorities, canary schedule, rollback triggers, and cost-latency tradeoffs.
- Create a lightweight decision rubric for switching lanes mid-quarter (metrics, approvals, required runbooks).
- Deliver a one-page executive summary and a companion dashboard spec for Console to visualize cohort exposure and unit economics.

Success metrics:
- Clear commit lanes accepted by PM, Eng, and Sales by 2025-02-14.
- Dashboard prototype wireframe submitted to Console team by 2025-02-21.
- Decision rubric tested in tabletop simulation with SRE (2 scenarios) by 2025-03-07.

Stakeholders:
- PM (owner): Aisha Patel
- Eng lead: Nikhil Rao (runtime)
- Console partner: Lena Zhou
- SRE: Omar Khan
- Solutions / Sales input: Priya Desai

Deliverables:
1) Scenario matrix (CSV + included reasoning)
2) Commitment playbook (one-pager + approval matrix)
3) Dashboard wireframe + metric list for Console team
4) Tabletop simulation notes and follow-up action list

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Capacity uncertainty in APAC regions may push enterprise cohorts onto regional fallbacks; scenario must enumerate fallback models and associated quality deltas.
- Aggressive lane reduces unit cost via larger-scale quantized variants but increases regression risk; include a require-list of prompt-based regression tests prior to rollout.
- Console telemetry currently has a 24hr lag for cohort breakdown; real-time decision triggers will initially rely on sampling traces rather than full telemetry.

Acceptance criteria:
- Matrix includes explicit model ID/version for each endpoint in all three scenarios.
- For each rollback trigger, responsible approver (role) and required artifacts (PR, eval report, SLO hit) are listed.
- Dashboard spec contains token-cost, median P95 latency, error rate, and sample-quality delta per cohort.

Risks:
- Customer confusion if cohort mapping changes mid-quarter — mitigate with advance comms templates and per-customer notices.
- Missing telemetry could delay detection of quality regressions; SRE to evaluate sampling thresholds.

Next steps:
- 2025-01-13: Kickoff with runtime and Console; collect workload profiles by cohort.
- 2025-01-20: Draft scenario matrix and share with Sales for cohort validity check.
- 2025-02-04: PM review and iterate; confirm canary windows.
- 2025-02-14: Stakeholder sign-off on selected scenario and contingency lanes.
